fatal_errors: The proposed Mg-Ti-Zr-Sc composition does not reconstruct the MgAlTiVFeCo alloy or its ball-milled BCC starting phase.
It does not identify SPS at 1000 °C as the optimum intervention and instead discusses an unsupported two-stage 800–850 °C/950–980 °C protocol.
It fails to define the requested lower-density and upper-volatility boundaries of 800 °C and 1000 °C.
The proposed mediator and mechanism omit the uniformly distributed AlV2O4, FeAl2O4, and FeTiO3 barrier phases, passive-film formation, chloride blocking, and biphasic parabolic oxidation.
No quantitative predictions are supplied for density, hardness, oxidation kinetics, or electrochemical behavior.
The falsification experiment lacks specified intermediate temperatures, an explicit 1000 °C comparator, measurable thresholds, and discriminating oxidation or corrosion parameters.
No prior evidence is cited for the asserted limitations of standard sintering.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad task of optimizing SPS for a lightweight Mg-transition-metal alloy and appropriately acknowledges uncertainty, but it does not provide the requested testable materials hypothesis. It changes the alloy chemistry, omits the BCC precursor, does not select the 1000 °C optimum, and leaves both critical temperature boundaries undefined. Its generic metastable-solid-solution mechanism is inconsistent with the target barrier-phase/passive-film mechanism, while the predicted outcomes and proposed comparison are too vague to falsify. The absence of supporting evidence and quantitative endpoints further prevents reconstruction or a well-supported plausible alternative.
